n.description: Number of nodes (customers) in the network

p.description: Number of nodes to be selected as medians

c.description: Service cost between every ordered pair of nodes; c_{ij} is the cost of serving node i from median j

assumptions.description: The number of medians to open is at least one and strictly less than the number of nodes.
The cost from any node to itself is zero.

code.python: assert all(c[i][i] == 0 for i in range(n))

assumptions.description: The cost between any two distinct nodes is strictly positive.
assumptions.formulation: c_{ij} > 0 \quad \forall i, j \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\},\ i \neq j

code.python: assert all(c[i][j] > 0 for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j)

G.description: For each node i, the number of distinct cost values c_{ij} in row i of the cost matrix.
G.formulation: G_i = |\{\, c_{ij} : 0 \leq j \leq n-1 \,\}| \quad \forall i \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\}

code.python: G = [len(set(c[i][j] for j in range(n))) for i in range(n)]

D.description: For each node i, the sorted list of distinct cost values in row i of the cost matrix. 0 = D_{i0} < D_{i1} < ... < D_{i,G_i-1} = max{c_{ij}}_{j=0}^{n-1}.
D.formulation: D_i = \mathrm{sort}(\{\, c_{ij} : 0 \leq j \leq n-1 \,\}) \quad \forall i \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\}

code.python: D = [sorted(set(c[i][j] for j in range(n))) for i in range(n)]

y.description: y_j is 1 if node j is selected as a median, 0 otherwise

z.description: z_{ik} is 1 if the allocation of cost of customer i is at least D_{ik} (no matter which median it is allocated to), 0 otherwise

constraints.description: Exactly p nodes are selected as medians.

code.gurobipy: model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(y[j] for j in range(n)) == p)

constraints.description: Covering constraint: if there is no median at less than distance D_{ik} from node i, then z_{ik} takes value 1.
constraints.formulation: z_{ik} + \sum_{j\,:\,c_{ij} < D_{ik}} y_j \geq 1 \quad \forall i \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\},\ \forall k \in \{1, \ldots, G_i - 1\}

objective.description: Minimize the total service cost, expressed as a telescoping sum of radius increments: each node i pays D[i][k] - D[i][k-1] for every threshold k (k >= 1) up to the cost at which it is first covered by an open median.

notes: This is the canonical representation (CR) of the p-median problem, given in Section 2 of garcia2011 (whose title calls it a 'radius formulation'). CR was introduced by Cornuejols et al. (1980) for the simple plant location problem and is adapted here to the p-median problem; it is the reduced, set-covering-based formulation on which garcia2011 builds its column-and-row generation algorithm. Instead of allocation variables x_{ij}, it uses a location variable y_j per node and cumulative variables z_{ik} that accumulate the cost of serving node i in telescoping increments over the distinct cost values D_{ik} of row i.

The paper indexes the cumulative variables z_{ik} and the thresholds D_{ik} with k = 1, ..., G_i over the sorted distinct row costs 0 = D_{i1} < D_{i2} < ... < D_{i{G_i}} = max_j c_{ij}, using z_{ik} only for k = 2, ..., G_i. Here everything is 0-indexed to match the Python arrays: D[i][0] = 0, ..., D[i][G_i-1] = max_j c_{ij}, and the covering constraint and objective range over k = 1, ..., G_i-1 (the paper's k = 2, ..., G_i). The unused z[i][0] corresponds to the paper's omitted z_{i1}.

The covering set {j : c_{ij} < D[i][k]} is the set of nodes that, if opened, would serve node i at a cost strictly below the threshold D[i][k]; this is the CR analogue of the CF linking constraint x_{ij} <= x_{jj}.

The paper defines z_ik as binary but notes that, since the objective coefficients are positive in a minimization, each z_{ik} is forced to 0 unless a covering constraint requires it to be 1; hence no upper bound is needed and the z_{ik} may equivalently be relaxed to nonnegative continuous variables. This formulation keeps them binary, matching the paper's original definition.
The problem-level parametrization (n, p, c) is used directly, so gen_params.py is a pass-through; the derived quantities G and D are formulation-level definitions computed from c.
